answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The lantern multiplier is published, charged in marble, and quartz lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2937 identities would post 4746 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
